requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE contact_id = 14 AND case_id <> 231 AND (assigned_to = 619 OR assignment_group_id = 63)

disagreement: selector and expected: A all seven other cases of contact 14 counted where assigned to user 619 or group 63 (expected 0), B the three other new cases 226, 228 and 246 counted where still unassigned (expected 3); chose A's because it covers every other case of the customer and tests exactly the assignee and group a wrongly chosen case would receive, whereas any other assignment of the new cases is not something this request touches

notes:
The membership row is not asked for in words; it follows from the policy rule that the assignee must belong to the assignment group, and the benchmark tests it.
The report check is a conjunction of the notification cells and the case's state, assignee and group, so it is carried by the notification requirement and jointly by the two case requirements.
The notification's knowledge_id is not fixed by the request or policy and is not tested.

disagreement: value: the boundary stay on the customer's other cases: one pass counts the seven other cases given Paul Moyer or Case Triage_4 (expected 0), the other counts the three other new cases that stay unassigned (expected 3); chose the first because it covers every other case and tests the exact values a wrongly chosen case would receive.
